newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strike call at Bank of France gets little support.
newsitem.headline: Strike call at Bank of France gets little support.

text.p: Few Bank of France employees heeded calls for a 24-hour strike on Tuesday, called by the three unions at the central bank during a meeting of a committee evenly split between management and worker representatives.

According to figures given by the Bank of France management, 12 percent of total employees stopped work. At its Paris headquarters 4.7 percent of the workforce went on strike while there was an 18.6 percent turnout at its branch network and a 4.1 percent following at its printing operations.
The unions did not give figures but acknowledged that the turnout had been limited.

The CFDT, CGT and SNA unions called the strike to protest against what they termed "pseudo-talks" about the future strategy of the central bank presented by Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet on October 4.

"They told us everything was negotiable, but in fact nothing is up for negotiation," a union member said. He said the unions had suspended their work with the management and workers committee from that date.
The committee met on Tuesday afternoon to try and resolve the situation. The unions said their differences were mainly about the future of units within the Bank's branch network.
Trichet said on October 5 the central bank expected to reduce the level of operations at a certain number of units although there were no definite plans yet.
